blockers.b3d_ground_truth: B3D (jnc*) is scored on automatic ground truth from the same detector family as Tetris and the reference; its numbers are provisional until R1.O1.
blockers.native_results: The scored exports (/sota-results/*/leap/, written 2026-04-10) were built from /data/alenachao/data/leap-dataset/outputs/parsed_results/<dataset>, which is not on ace. ace holds an earlier run for CalDoT1/2 only (/work/alenachao/tunnel/work/LEAP/outputs/parsed_results/caldot1 and caldot2, 2026-03-12). Rebuilding every export from it with the logic of export-leap-outputs.py's reconstruct_tracks_json, in memory, and comparing the parsed JSON with the scored exports matches 3 of 49 non-empty CalDoT1 and 2 of 56 non-empty CalDoT2 exports, plus 7 of 11 and 4 of 4 empty ones. The check ran once on 2026-10-26 in a throwaway container with both directories mounted read-only; it is not part of this script, because the polyis container does not mount /work/alenachao/tunnel/work. The earlier run is therefore not the scored run. Without the scored run's results.json, both ends of the ambiguous objects and which objects' patterns were resampled, repeated, or truncated are unknown. The DetA lost between count_ceiling and LEAP's DetA (attribution.deta_decomposition.placement_loss_abs) mixes the exporter's pattern placement, LEAP's own pattern choice, and any time-base mismatch, and cannot be split.
blockers.raw_and_linear_interpolation_variants: LEAP's raw sparse observations (the boxes its detector found on the frames it sampled, with re-identification ids) are not on ace: the exporter reads only intervals and motion patterns, the scored exports hold only pattern boxes, and /work/alenachao/tunnel/work/LEAP/outputs/reid/caldot1 and caldot2 are empty. The planned 'raw' (only observed boxes) and 'linear interpolation' (interpolation between observed boxes instead of pattern placement) HOTA variants cannot be scored.
blockers.time_base: The frame base of LEAP's intervals cannot be confirmed on ace, since the scored run's inputs are not here. LEAP's configs (LEAP/configs/jnc*.yaml, caldot*.yaml) set fps 15, as our clips. ace's copies of LEAP's B3D test videos (/work/alenachao/tunnel/work/LEAP/data/videos/jnc0, jnc2, jnc6, jnc7 /test) are 29 fps with 2150, 1876-1877, 2077, and 2090 frames, about twice our 15-fps clips (1075, 938-939, 1038-1039, and 1045 frames), while its CalDoT copies are 15 fps with 900 frames, as ours (ffprobe packet counts, 2026-10-26, throwaway container with the directory mounted read-only). Whether the scored B3D run read the 29-fps copies is unknown; datasets[*].time_base records what the counts suggest.

findings.attribution: The conversion steps measured here (the p140 fix, dropping the ambiguous objects, and scoring full clips) move LEAP's HOTA by summary.measured_conversion_effect_range. They do not cover the core of the conversion, the exporter placing LEAP's motion pattern over each interval (resampled, repeated, or truncated). That step, LEAP's own pattern choice, and any time-base mismatch together make up the DetA lost between count_ceiling and LEAP's DetA (datasets[*].attribution.deta_decomposition), so the error the placement introduces is bounded above by that loss, not measured. Which of counts and placement loses more DetA depends on the scale (summary.count_loss_larger_absolute, summary.placement_loss_larger_log). AssA is not attributed, since no bound here constrains it. This does not support saying that the conversion introduces little error.
findings.count_ids: TrackEval's Count IDs (and p142's Count_TracksMAPE) is max(track id) + 1 per clip, not the number of tracks; box_frames.*.objects_in_clip counts distinct ids.
findings.scored_window: polyis/trackeval/dataset.py with TrackEval scores a clip only on its first min(T_gt, T_tracker) frames when both sides have boxes (see datasets[*].scored_window). For LEAP it hides misses after its last exported box. evaluation/p110_accuracy_compute.py uses the same dataset class, so the reference, Tetris, and OTIF are scored the same way; they are not quantified here. The *_full_length TrackEval variants score full clips.
findings.time_base: Every interval, clipping, ceiling, and attribution number assumes LEAP's frame f is the clip's frame f. On the datasets in summary.time_base_flagged, LEAP's counts correlate better with the ground truth under another time scale (datasets[*].time_base), and their exports run past the clip; there the boxes past the clip, the end-clipped shares, the count ceiling, and the attribution may reflect a frame-base mismatch rather than LEAP's intervals, until someone with the scored run's inputs confirms the frame base (blockers.time_base).

method.attribution: measured steps: fix_effect, ambiguous_dropped_effect(_full_length), full_length_effect; deta_decomposition: 1 - DetA = (1 - ceiling) + (ceiling - DetA) on full clips, and -ln DetA = -ln ceiling + ln(ceiling / DetA); the placement part mixes the exporter, LEAP's pattern choice, and any time-base mismatch; AssA not attributed
method.box_changes: surplus of the old cache over the fixed one over the whole file and inside the clip (frames < n); gap_fill = old cache boxes - raw export boxes, asserted equal to the frames between each wrapped object's head and tail
method.chain: LEAP results.json/tracks.json -> export-leap-outputs.py (pattern resampled, repeated, or truncated over [start, end); negative starts wrap to the list end) -> p140 (since 2026-10-26: wrapped tail dropped, full-span objects kept whole as ambiguous, frames >= clip length dropped, unwrap.json) -> p141 (TrackEval vs root 003_groundtruth) -> p142 tradeoff.csv
method.clipped_share: start-clipped = wrapped; end-clipped = a known interval end > clip length n (never ambiguous); *_upper adds the ambiguous objects that may be clipped at that end (any at the start, those of exports longer than n at the end); either end: lower adds the ambiguous objects of exports longer than n (clipped at one end for certain), upper adds every ambiguous object
method.count_ceiling: M = sum over clip frames of min(p, g); DetA <= M / (G + P - M) for any box placement and any alpha; HOTA <= sqrt(DetA bound)
method.hota_summary: means over the 19 alphas as p142 computes HOTA_HOTA; alpha_0.05 holds the loosest threshold; HOTA_TP/FN/FP only at alpha 0.05
method.input_digests: per source: file count, bytes, latest mtime, SHA-256 over sorted "video<TAB>file SHA-256" lines
method.interval_recovery: one run [a, b] -> [a, b + 1); head run from 0 plus tail run ending at L - 1 -> [tail_start - L, head_end + 1); one run over the whole export -> ambiguous; checked per clip against unwrap.json's ids and box counts
method.scored_window: a file is as long as its largest frame_idx + 1; with boxes on both sides a clip is scored on min(T_gt, T_tracker) frames; checked against DATASET.json at alpha 0.05
method.time_base: assumed: LEAP frame f = clip frame f (LEAP configs fps 15, clips 15 fps); checked by export length / clip length, LEAP's median interval / the ground truth's median track length, and the median per-clip Pearson correlation of LEAP's per-frame interval counts (LEAP frames >= 0) with the ground truth's, clip frame t reading LEAP frame round(t / s), s in 0.4-1.5 by 0.05; flagged when the best s is not 1 and gains more than 0.05; shifts at s = 1 are the native-queries lags (native_queries.lag_correlations)

trackeval.full_length: tracks and ground truth cut to frames < n and padded with an empty row on frame n - 1
trackeval.metrics: HOTA, CLEAR, Identity (threshold 0.5), Count, configured as p141
trackeval.output: temporary directory, removed after the run; only summaries are kept
